key_insight: Scale-driven averaging reduces uncertainty in panel ultimate load, but spatially correlated interface variability remains essential for predicting early damage initiation and location.
engineering_relevance: Match model complexity to the design criterion: spatially uniform variability for global load capacity and correlated random fields for local skin–stringer bond integrity.
method: Extend likelihood-free Bayesian calibration to Mode II fracture using experimental coupon data.
Propagate interface variability from coupons to aerospace panels using simulation-based stochastic finite elements.
Compare B-basis design, spatially uniform variability, and spatially correlated random fields.
evidence_signal: Coupon experiments inform stochastic calibration, while panel simulations show uncertainty attenuation in ultimate load and sensitivity of early damage to local weak spots.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative errors or panel-level experimental validation, leaving predictive accuracy and transferability to other structures unresolved.
paper_title: Scaling of Interface Variability in Aerospace Composite Structures: A Multi-scale Stochastic Approach from Local Identification to Panel Response
